quest.title: The Grave of the Guarded
quest.description: You have an unexpected reunion with Dainsleif within The Chasm. After getting wind of the situation, you believe that this place must be intimately linked to the Abyss Order, and thus begin investigating...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x725, Mora x25825, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Investigate the ruins ahead and find a path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are signs of hilichurl activity here. Could these be the hilichurls the requester was talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Requester? ...In fact, hold on. You still haven't told me what you're doing here. I doubt that most travelers would have any reason to venture down this way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We took a commission from the Adventurers' Guild to investigate The Chasm. Apparently, a whole load of hilichurls have been gathering here, and the requester wants to know why.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And now, it looks like we've finally found our first clue...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Do you want the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean, you know something about this?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: As it happens, I do.

choices.text: Huh? Did I miss something?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's understandable that you did not perceive anything unusual. What makes this place so strange is that...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...the environment here weakens the effect of the curse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The curse? Oh! Paimon remembers, last time you guys were saying that Khaenri'ah's people were cursed to immortality or something...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: For centuries, I have suffered daily from the curse that was laid upon me. But here... I suddenly feel a small amount of relief from this suffering.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And right here, right now, I can feel my body sending a strong message to me... It is telling me, "stay."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this place weakens the curse? That's pretty incredible, but how?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That I shall need to investigate. But to the best of my knowledge, the Abyss Order does not have the technology to achieve this.

choices.text: So you're saying...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Indeed. Do you know why hilichurls wear masks?

choices.text: I think so?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's to hide their appearance, lest they catch sight of their reflection in a body of water...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Compared to how they remember themselves, it is a terrible sight to behold, one that causes them great despair.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So these hilichurls really are from...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The curse of "immortality" denies death to those afflicted with it... and yet, it does not truly mean that they will never die.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean, there's a way to undo it?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: No. I mean that the body and soul will continue to be eroded until they are virtually nonexistent, even if "death" is not the form that this erosion takes.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: When the hilichurls realize that the end is nigh for them, it seems their instinct is to seek out a calm and dark corner of the world in which to finally say goodbye to the centuries of suffering they have endured.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And of all the places they could lay down to rest, one that can ease the effects of their curse would surely be their first choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... That's so...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Conversation's over, brace yourselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What is it!?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: We're under attack.

choices.text: I'm not sure...
The hilichurls that come here are also from...
Does this have anything to do with the upside-down city?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What were those? And why did they attack us all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Black Serpent Knights. They once belonged to the Royal Guard of Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second! Royal Guard? So... they used to be your troops!?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Yes, they were. But now, the curse engulfs them, and they fight with none of the honor they once had...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because they've become pawns of the Abyss now?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Let's continue on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Dain...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Seems we missed one...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Wait, stand down. There's something different about this one...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...It's disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck? What was going on with that one? Was it trying to say something?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: (How is this possible... How could he have retained self-awareness for 500 years without... it?)

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: (But more importantly, why did he seem so familiar...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he recognized you.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: That would be a miraculous outcome indeed for a cataclysm that brought total doom and destruction... Or perhaps it was just a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: We should press onward, to the city.

talks.objective: Go to the entrance to the ruins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like there's a strange energy surrounding the city. We can't go any further.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess there should be a mechanism or something around here, right? Traveler, looks like it's time to get into ruin-exploring mode!

choices.text: Puzzle time, huh.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Don't waste your time.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Khaenri'ah's technology, Abyssal power... Two things I couldn't be more familiar with. They're just cheap tricks to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! So the Abyss Order really is trying to hide something here, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Dain seems like he really understands what's going on here. No wonder the Abyss Order doesn't want him around.

choices.text: Was this upside-down city built by Khaenri'ah?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Not necessarily. The closer we draw, the more I am inclined to conclude that these ruins belong to a more ancient civilization still.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Abyss Order simply got to them before anyone else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even older than Khaenri'ah? Whoa, Paimon can't even imagine back that far...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That said, the architecture here does somewhat resemble that of Khaenri'ah... At least, it would if it were the other way up.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Let's head toward the light over there. Mind your footing on the way ahead. It's a long way down.

choices.text: Was this upside-down city built by the Abyss Order?
I'll take a look around and see what I can find.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So there's no Abyss Order secrets to be found here... Just a bunch of hilichurls nearing the end of their existence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We probably shouldn't disturb them.

talks.objective: Go to the lit room in the ruins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah, Black Serpent Knights!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this where they're based? Or wait, are they guarding something here?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: We are likely drawing near to whatever the Abyss Order is trying to hide. Let's take them out first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, more Black Serpent Knights!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, they're not coming after us. Are they just trying to scare us off?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These knights seem like they're hiding something behind them...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hold on, I think they...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah, they're coming! Quick, get them!

talks.objective: Examine what the Black Serpent Knights were protecting

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...So the Black Serpent Knights have nothing to do with the Abyss Order's secret. Huh, I should have guessed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what exactly is going on with these hilichurls?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: As I said, for these hilichurls, the end is nigh.

choices.text: The hilichurls are preparing to meet their end...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They have grown old and fearful of the light, even become one with the darkness. And yet the curse continues to corrode them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why would the Black Serpent Knights wanna stay here and guard them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aah! More of them are closing in!

choices.text: Let's try to avoid fighting them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...It's him! The guy that came out of nowhere and disappeared again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And now they're retreating... Did he just order them to do that?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...Halfdan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, whoa, what? You recognize him?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...Could it be... If it's as I suspect, then this is a truly tragic state of affairs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dain?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: You want to know why they were gathered here guarding the hilichurls, don't you?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It's because as far as the Black Serpent Knights are concerned, they are simply doing their duty.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The one who ordered them to retreat just now... I suddenly recognized him. I knew him as a young man, an elite in the Royal Guard of old... His name is "Halfdan."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So he's from 500 years ago, too...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: To this day, I still remember the final orders I, the Twilight Sword, gave to Halfdan on the day of disaster in Khaenri'ah, before I made haste back to the palace...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: "Inform all Black Serpent Knights to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs."

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Because we, of course, were royal guards. But this would mean nothing in the events that followed... Royals, gentry, common folk, these identities made no difference.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Against the might of the gods, the only identity that mattered was being from Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: These Black Serpent Knights have lost their intellect. But perhaps, in whatever remains of their minds, they are still protecting the people of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: If you see these ruins as Khaenri'ah in the throes of disaster, and these hilichurls as the people crying for help...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...then suddenly, I can make sense of what I'm hearing. Their growls are less of a threat and more of a warning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then... what are they saying?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Though it is barely discernible, I can just about make it out. They keep repeating a word from the old language of Khaenri'ah... "Run."

choices.text: So they're not talking to us...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Even I have to admit, the fact their will is strong enough to survive 500 years of erosion... It is nothing short of a miracle born from hopelessness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So Paimon had them all wrong...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: It doesn't matter. Even I took them for enemies for a moment.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Let's keep heading toward the light at the top. I believe the Black Serpent Knights will no longer try to stop us.

choices.text: So they're telling the hilichurls behind them to escape...
Fighting them is meaningless.

talks.objective: Go to the chamber at the center of the ruins' summit
Go to the chamber at the center of the ruins' summit
Go to the chamber at the center of the ruins' summit
Go to the chamber at the center of the ruins' summit

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey look, there's no door sealing this room off. Looks like we can finally head to the room in the center.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, up there! A water pool!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even the water pool is upside-down. Wow! This is a pretty amazing place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dain, do you have any idea at all how it works?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The pool must be part of the entire city structure, a relic of this ancient civilization.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: And more importantly... it is the very thing that is weakening the curse.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Here, my whole body feels more at peace than it has in a long time. The effect is stronger here than it was before, and I think it's because that water pool has something akin to a cleansing effect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cleansing? So that means... the water in that pool can wash away the curse for good?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No. That would be impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are you so sure?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I have lived with this curse for 500 years, and I have been fully conscious the entire time... Suffice to say, no one understands the curse like I do.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It is a way of branding us at the level of the fate of the world itself. When a god applies a curse, it takes effect at a higher level of reality than the person themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Even now, I can feel the curse slowly permeating my entire being, becoming part of me, slowly but surely replacing me.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Perhaps it may be possible to suppress the corrosive effect of the curse for a time, but cleansing it entirely...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Consider it tantamount to burning away an integral part of your body. It is not a process that one could ever hope to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Cleansing the curse costs you your life? Whoa... An irreversible curse, Paimon can't even imagine...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: In any case, I can feel that the water's cleansing effect is not nearly potent enough. At most, it might suppress the curse but a little.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? So what's that contraption there? It looks kinda out of place...

choices.text: An Abyss Order device?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Frankly, I have never seen a device of this design before either. It is not unreasonable to suspect that it could belong to the Abyss Order. But what could they be planning to do here...
(*clunk* *clunk*...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes! That gave Paimon a fright... So all the doors are open now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah, Halfdan's back again...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Halfdan. Do you have something to say to me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He ran off... but he didn't disappear like last time!

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: He's indicating that we should follow him. Are you coming?

choices.text: This could be a useful lead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True... So, uh... We going, then?

choices.text: He doesn't seem to hold any malice toward us.
Perhaps it's the Abyss Order's secret.

talks.objective: Go to the chamber at the center of the ruins' summit

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: More hilichurls. And they look really well-protected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All these hilichurls want is to quietly fade away in peace... Paimon hopes they can get their final wish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's never seen such well-behaved hilichurls before. Paimon wonders if it has anything to do with being an old soul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, that was the last of them! Now, let's see what it was they were trying to hide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dain... Why so quiet?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I'm just thinking, nothing more. If you're trying to console me, I can assure you there is no need.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Fine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey look, vines. You should be able to climb up, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Halfdan jumped down over there. Let's follow him.
